newsitem.title: THAILAND: Burmese troops, students said in border clashes.
newsitem.headline: Burmese troops, students said in border clashes.

text.p: Burmese soldiers have attacked rebel students near the border with Thailand, members of the student group said on Friday.

"The troops of the State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) have begun an offensive against an ABSDF camp on the Burma side of the border opposite Thailand's Thap Sakae in Prachuab Kirikhan province," said a statement by the All Burma Students' Democratic Front (ABSDF).
Prachuab Kirikhan is about 280 km (170 miles) southwest of Bangkok.
But a military official in Rangoon said he had not heard of any offensive being launched and that he did not think the ABSDF had any camps inside Burma.

Aung Thu Nyein, general secretary of the ABSDF, told Reuters the camp housed about 150 people, most of them armed fighters. He said some family members and residents of a neighbouring village had fled to Thailand to escape the fighting.
He said nine SLORC soldiers had been killed and six injured, but said the ABSDF had suffered no casualties.
"Well, they must be supermen then," said the Burmese official. "This shows me it must be a fabrication. Even if there were skirmishes there would be casualties on both sides."

The ABSDF is an umbrella organization that was founded on the border in 1988 by groups of students who fled the military's bloody supression of nationwide pro-democracy demonstrations in September that year.
Disease and fighting have depleted the ranks of the student groups over the past nine years, but they and other rebel groups have continued a low-level guerrilla war against the SLORC.
